correctness.rationale: For all real \(T>0\) and \(w\in[0,1]\), the normalized Hermite ambiguity gain equals \(e^{-s}[(1-w)+w(1-2s+s^2/2)^2]\). The exact Laguerre factorization and derivative establish all stationary signs. The cubic at \(w=1/4\) has one real root in \((6,7)\), proving a protected minimum at \(s=4\) up to the unique exit \(T_*\). For \(T>T_*\), the active interior branch decreases strictly with \(w\) whereas the outer endpoint increases strictly, giving a unique intersection. All boundary regimes \(T=2,4,T_*\), weights zero and one, and the large-radius asymptotics are proved analytically. An independent standard-library checker verifies exact polynomial identities and numerical Hermite ambiguity integrals; finite tests are supplementary, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The weighted squared Gaussian/second-Hermite ambiguity multiplier is the exact pointwise least-squares inversion denominator under a fixed channel-precision budget. A sharp and motivated design transition occurs: the precise quarter-weighted design protects the worst-case squared margin \(e^{-4}\) as the dimensionless disk radius expands from \(T=4\) to \(T_*=8.8327355\ldots\). After this plateau, a unique interior/endpoint contact determines the allocation and leads to the sharp large-radius law \(\Gamma(T)\sim T^4e^{-T}/4\). These are meaningful nontrivial decisions for window budgeting rather than a repackaging of the known Hermite ambiguity formula.
